description: Advanced C++ Exam Challenge: Output-Based Questions, OOP, STL, Templates, Pointers and Tricky Concepts

questions.questionText: What is the output? int x = 5; cout << x++ << " " << x;
questions.explanation: Post-increment first produces 5 and then increases x to 6.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int x = 5; cout << ++x << " " << x;
questions.explanation: Pre-increment increases x before its value is used, so both outputs are 6.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int a = 10, b = 20; cout << (a > b ? a : b);
questions.explanation: The condition a > b is false, so the conditional operator returns b, which is 20.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int a = 5; int& r = a; r = 10; cout << a;
questions.explanation: r is a reference to a. Assigning 10 to r changes a to 10.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int a = 10; int* p = &a; *p = 25; cout << a;
questions.explanation: p points to a, so assigning 25 through *p changes the value of a to 25.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int arr[] = {10, 20, 30, 40}; cout << *(arr + 2);
questions.explanation: arr + 2 points to the third element, so dereferencing it gives 30.

questions.questionText: What is the output? string s = "C++"; cout << s.length();
questions.explanation: The string C++ contains three characters: C, + and +.

questions.questionText: What is the output? vector<int> v = {1, 2, 3}; v.push_back(4); cout << v.size();
questions.explanation: The vector initially has three elements. push_back(4) adds one more, making its size 4.

questions.questionText: What is the output? stack<int> s; s.push(10); s.push(20); cout << s.top();
questions.explanation: A stack follows LIFO, so the last pushed element, 20, is at the top.

questions.questionText: What is the output? queue<int> q; q.push(10); q.push(20); cout << q.front();
questions.explanation: A queue follows FIFO, so the first inserted element, 10, is at the front.

questions.questionText: What is the output? set<int> s = {3, 1, 2, 2}; cout << s.size();
questions.explanation: A set stores only unique values. The values are 1, 2 and 3, so its size is 3.

questions.questionText: What is the output? map<int, string> m; m[1] = "C"; cout << m[1];
questions.explanation: The key 1 is associated with the string C, so m[1] returns C.

questions.questionText: Which concept allows a derived class to provide its own implementation of a virtual function?
questions.explanation: Function overriding allows a derived class to provide a different implementation of an inherited virtual function.

questions.questionText: What is the output? class A { public: virtual void show(){ cout << "A"; } }; class B: public A { public: void show() override { cout << "B"; } }; A* p = new B; p->show();
questions.explanation: Because show() is virtual, the call through the base pointer invokes B::show().

questions.questionText: Which statement about a pure virtual function is correct?
questions.explanation: A pure virtual function is declared by assigning = 0.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int a = 10; int b = 20; swap(a, b); cout << a << " " << b;
questions.explanation: std::swap exchanges the values of a and b.

questions.questionText: Which STL algorithm is commonly used to sort a range of elements?
questions.explanation: std::sort() is the standard STL algorithm used to sort elements in a range.

questions.questionText: What is the output? template<typename T> T square(T x) { return x * x; } cout << square(5);
questions.explanation: The function template is instantiated for int, and square(5) returns 25.

questions.questionText: Which C++ feature allows a class to inherit from more than one base class?
questions.explanation: Multiple inheritance allows one derived class to inherit from two or more base classes.

questions.questionText: What is the output? class A { public: A(){ cout << "A"; } }; class B: public A { public: B(){ cout << "B"; } }; int main(){ B obj; }
questions.explanation: The base-class constructor executes before the derived-class constructor.

questions.questionText: Which function is automatically called when an object is destroyed?
questions.explanation: The destructor is automatically called when an object's lifetime ends.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int x = 10; try { if (x == 10) throw x; } catch (int n) { cout << n; }
questions.explanation: The value 10 is thrown and caught by the catch block as an int.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly releases an array allocated using new[]?
questions.explanation: Memory allocated using new[] should be released using delete[].

questions.questionText: Which special member function is used to initialize a new object from an existing object of the same class?
questions.explanation: A copy constructor initializes a new object from an existing object of the same class.

questions.questionText: Which statement about C++ is correct?
questions.optionA: C++ supports both procedural and object-oriented programming
questions.explanation: C++ is a multi-paradigm language and supports procedural, object-oriented, generic and other programming styles.
